promptState.text: Keep the woman, her pose and the framing of <image1> exactly as they are, and dress her in the black PIXA t-shirt and the blue jeans from <image2>. Keep her face, hair and body shape, the original background and the original lighting. The clothes fit naturally, with realistic fabric texture and natural folds. High fashion editorial photography, sharp details.

{"version": 1, "content": "

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the list in the note above.

  • Load Diffusion Model (Qwen Image 2.1) - The image model itself, 7B, from Alibaba's Qwen team.
  • Load CLIP (Qwen3-VL 8B) - Reads your prompt and looks at your pictures.
  • Load VAE - Turns pictures into the model's own format and back. It works with four channels, red, green, blue and transparency, which is how this model can hand back a transparent picture.
  • LoRA Loader Pixaroma - Adds Viggle's turbo LoRA, which lets the model finish a picture in 6 steps instead of 25. It has no trigger word. Keep it at strength 1.

 The numbers you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you have to touch.

  • 1. Load Image - Character - The picture you are editing. In the prompt it is <image1>.
  • 2. Load Image - Outfit - A second picture the model can take things from. In the prompt it is <image2>. Its loader scales it to about 1 megapixel, the size the model reads it at.
  • 3. Pick Orientation and Size - The size and shape of the result. Picture 1 always goes to the model whole. Pick the shape closest to it (the demo picture is 9:16, so 768 x 1376) and the result lines up with it in the Compare; pick another shape and the model re-frames the picture to fit it. The starred sizes are Qwen's native 2K ones and much slower.
  • 4. Add a prompt - What to change, and what to keep. Name the pictures as <image1> and <image2>.
  • 5. Seed Random/Fixed? - Fixed repeats the same result, Random rolls a new one each Run.

 The speed nodes

Teal, above the graph.

  • Qwen Image 2.1 Cache - Where the model keeps what it has already worked out about your pictures and the prompt, so it does not redo that on every step. Leave it on auto / default. The note of the normal Outfit Change workflow in this folder says when to change it.
  • Model Attention Backend - Set to comfy kitchen attention, a faster way to do the model's attention maths. It changes the speed, not the picture. On a graphics card that cannot use it, ComfyUI falls back to normal attention by itself.

 The helpers

Purple. They run by themselves.

  • Math Expression - Works out how many megapixels the size from step 3 has, so picture 1 is read at the same number of pixels as the result.
  • Scale Image to Total Pixels - Works out the size picture 1 is read at: that many pixels, in steps of 32, in picture 1's own shape. Only that size is used.
  • Get Image Size - Reads that size as a width and a height for Resize Crop Pixaroma under it.
  • Resize Crop Pixaroma - Scales picture 1 to that size and trims the few pixels that do not fit, so the model gets the whole picture and nothing is stretched.
  • ModelSamplingFlux - Spaces the 6 steps for the size from step 3, the way the turbo LoRA was trained. The name says Flux because the maths is the same. Its two numbers are set for this LoRA (max shift 0.69, base shift 0.5): leave them.

 The render

Green. These run by themselves.

  • Text Encode Qwen Image 2.1 - Reads your prompt and both pictures. Its resolution is set to 0, which takes the pictures as they come: picture 1 from the helpers, picture 2 at about 1 megapixel from its loader. Its negative prompt box does nothing at CFG 1, the setting this model is made for, so leave it empty.
  • Empty Latent Image - The blank canvas for the result, at the size from step 3. The encoder's own canvas would always copy picture 1's shape.
  • RandomNoise, KSamplerSelect, BasicScheduler, ExtendIntermediateSigmas, Basic Guider, SamplerCustomAdvanced - Together they do the job of a KSampler, with the 6 steps the turbo LoRA wants. BasicScheduler makes the 4 steps the LoRA was trained on, and ExtendIntermediateSigmas cuts the first, biggest one into three. Basic Guider means CFG 1, the setting this model is made for, so there is no negative prompt. Leave their numbers as they are.
  • VAE Decode - Turns the finished render into a picture.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Image Compare Pixaroma - Picture 1, as the model saw it, and the result, one over the other. Move the mouse across it to slide between them.
  • Preview Image Pixaroma - Shows the result and saves it to your output folder as a PNG.

The dark Run Timer above them shows how long the last Run took.

widgets_values:
{"version": 1, "content": "

SETTINGS AND RUN TIME

 What this workflow makes

The Outfit Change workflow in 6 steps instead of 25, with Viggle's turbo LoRA: about three times as fast at native 2K, with results that look the same. Picture 2 is a reference the model takes things from: here, the outfit.

Tested on 8 seeds against the normal Outfit Change workflow on the same seeds: every turbo result kept the woman, her pose and the framing, and dressed her in the rock band t-shirt and the jeans from picture 2, lettering included, just like the normal ones.

Every number below was measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow and its own settings, each run on a fresh seed with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: the cost goes up with the pixels.

 How long a Run takes

SizePixelsTurbo: new pictures / new seedNormal: new pictures / new seed
768 x 1376about 1 MP, the demo's 9:166 s / 4 s11 s / 9 s
1536 x 1536about 2.4 MP, square13 s / 8 s25 s / 20 s
1536 x 2752native 2K, 9:1626 s / 16 s53 s / 43 s

Change a picture or the prompt and the model reads both pictures again, which is the first number; change only the seed and it reuses what it read, which is the second. The normal numbers are the Outfit Change workflow in this folder, measured in the same session.

 When to use the normal workflow

Viggle's model card says complicated edits can still fall short of the full model: many pictures at once, face swaps, instructions with several conditions, and small text. For those, use the normal Outfit Change workflow in this folder. For everything else, the turbo is the quick way to try prompts and seeds.

 Why the six green sampler nodes

The turbo LoRA was trained on 4 steps, and Viggle recommends cutting the first, biggest step into three: 6 steps. The six green nodes do that, which a plain KSampler cannot. ModelSamplingFlux spaces the steps for the result's size: in the Turbo Text to Image tests, 2K pictures came out with grainy fur without it.

 Picking the size

Picture 1 always goes to the model whole, read at the same number of pixels as the result. Pick the shape closest to it and the result lines up with it in the Compare: the demo picture is 9:16, so 768 x 1376. Pick another shape and the model re-frames the picture to fit.

 Kitchen attention

The teal Model Attention Backend node is set to comfy kitchen attention, a faster way to do the attention maths. On the same seed at 1536 x 2752, it took 16 s, against 23 s with the normal pytorch attention, and the two pictures came out as the same woman in the same pose and outfit, with small differences in the fine details. To compare it yourself, switch the node to pytorch attention.

It needs an Nvidia or AMD graphics card. On anything else ComfyUI falls back to normal attention by itself, so the workflow still runs.

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI has to load 6.8 GB of image model and 8.7 GB of text encoder, plus the turbo LoRA. Measured on a 768 x 1376 edit: 10 s with the models unloaded first, 4 s once they were loaded.

That was with the model files still in this machine's file cache. The very first load after switching the computer on reads them off the disk for real and will be slower; that case was not measured, so no number is given for it.

 What it takes off the card

The graphics card peaked at about 20 GB during these runs, at 1536 x 1536. ComfyUI keeps the models loaded while it has room, so that number says a 24 GB card copes, not how little the model can get by with.

 Writing the prompt

Name the pictures as <image1> and <image2>, and say what should stay the same as well as what should change. The demo prompt is the Outfit Change one, word for word.

Turbo LoRA model card
